scope: Only the roles named in this round of requirements: Bidder (bid increment ladder) and System (scheduled start and close of auctions). Status names map to the existing schema: spec 'new' = 'upcoming', spec 'close' = 'ended'.

roles.bidder: A signed-in customer who places bids on auctions.
roles.system: Scheduled background jobs that run without a user (start and close auctions).

features.title: Price-tiered bid increment
features.user_visible_behavior: The minimum next bid is the current price plus an increment that depends on the current price: $0.50 when the price is $1 up to $10, $1 from $10 up to $50, and larger steps above that. The auction page shows the correct minimum next bid, and a bid below it is rejected with a message stating the minimum.
verification: Unit: the increment for prices 1.00, 9.99, 10.00, 49.99, 50.00, 99.99, 100.00, 999.99, 1000.00 and 5000.00 matches the ladder (lower bound inclusive, upper bound exclusive).
Unit: the next minimum bid on an auction with no bids is its initial price; with bids it is the current price plus the ladder increment.
API: on an auction at $9.50, a bid of $9.99 is rejected with a message naming $10.00 as the minimum, and a bid of $10.00 is accepted.
API: on an auction at $10.00, a bid of $10.50 is rejected and a bid of $11.00 is accepted.
E2E: the auction page shows the minimum next bid from the ladder and updates after a bid is placed.

features.title: Start auction job
features.user_visible_behavior: A scheduled job runs every hour. Each run finds auctions in status 'upcoming' (spec: 'new') whose start time has arrived and sets them to 'active', so they appear as live and accept bids.
verification: Unit: the job switches an 'upcoming' auction whose start time is now or earlier to 'active'.
Unit: the job leaves alone 'upcoming' auctions with a future start time, plus 'cancelled' and 'ended' auctions.
Unit: running the job twice in a row changes nothing on the second run.
Integration: on startup the scheduler registers the job with a default interval of 1 hour; the interval can be set by config (e.g. AUCTION_JOB_INTERVAL_MS) so tests can run it fast.
E2E: an auction created with a start time a few seconds ahead shows as 'upcoming', then as 'active' after the job runs.
evidence: 2026-10-16 Unit: be/tests/job.start.test.ts startDueAuctions activates upcoming auctions with start_time <= now (incl. exactly now); future-start, cancelled and ended untouched; a second run returns 0 and leaves the row unchanged

2026-10-16 Integration: be/src/lib/scheduler.ts registers start-auctions at 3,600,000 ms by default, AUCTION_JOB_INTERVAL_MS overrides; runs at startup and every interval (fake timers); a failing run is logged and later ticks continue. server.ts starts it

2026-10-16 E2E: e2e/sys-001-start-job.spec.ts (API server with AUCTION_JOB_INTERVAL_MS=1000) auction starting in 4s shows 'upcoming', stored status flips to 'active' (GET /api/dev/auctions/:id/raw), page then shows 'active'
2026-10-16 vitest 16 files / 76 tests pass, be tsc ok, fe build ok, Playwright 16/16 pass
features.notes: The spec says 'start time equal to current time'. An hourly job would almost never hit an exact match, so the check is start_time <= now. Today 'active' is only derived at read time (effectiveStatus); after this job it should also be written to the DB.

features.title: Close auction job and settlement
features.user_visible_behavior: A scheduled job runs every hour. Each run finds 'active' auctions whose close date (start date + duration) has passed and closes them. If the highest bid is at least the reserve price, that bid wins: the winner's credit is debited by the bid amount and the seller's credit is credited with the bid amount minus the system commission. If the reserve is not met, or there are no bids, nobody wins and every hold is released. The auction status becomes 'ended' (spec: 'close').
verification: Unit: an 'active' auction past its close date with a top bid >= reserve is set to 'ended'; that bid is marked 'won' and the auction's winner is recorded.
Unit: the winner's balance goes down by the winning amount, and the seller's goes up by the amount minus commission; both changes have ledger rows.
Unit: a top bid below the reserve leaves no winner, releases every bidder's hold and sets the status to 'ended'; an auction with no bids is also 'ended' with no winner.
Unit: the job does not touch auctions that are not yet due.
Unit: concurrent or repeated runs settle each auction exactly once.
Integration: on startup the scheduler registers the job with a default interval of 1 hour, configurable for tests.
API: bids on an auction whose close date has passed are rejected even before the job has closed it.
E2E: the winner and seller see the correct balances and the auction shows as ended after the job runs.
evidence: 2026-10-16 Unit: be/tests/job.close.test.ts (SETTLE_ON_REQUEST=0, so only the job closes): due auction with top bid >= reserve -> ended, ticket won, winner_id set, settlement 'settled'; winner balance 1000->800, seller +200-commission, payment/payout ledger rows; reserve not met -> ended, no winner, holds released, 'reserve_not_met'; no bids -> 'no_bids'; not-yet-due untouched; 3 concurrent runs settle 3 auctions exactly once (3 settlements, 3 payments)
2026-10-16 Integration: scheduler registers close-auctions at 3,600,000 ms by default (AUCTION_JOB_INTERVAL_MS override); server.ts no longer runs its own 5s closer
2026-10-16 API: bid after close date with the job not yet run -> 400 'This auction has ended' while stored status is still 'active'

features.notes: Most of this logic already exists in be/src/lib/settlement.ts (settleAuction / closeDueAuctions), but it runs before every /api request and every 5s. Move it to the hourly scheduler. Open decision: keep the per-request settlement as a safety net so results are not delayed up to an hour (recommended), or rely on the hourly job only as the spec says. Use the tiered commission from sys-003.

features.title: Tiered system commission
features.user_visible_behavior: The commission taken from the seller's proceeds is a percentage of the winning price: 10% below $100, 5% from $100 to $999.99, 2% from $1,000 to $9,999.99, and 1% from $10,000 up. The seller's ledger entry shows the commission that was deducted.
verification: Unit: settlement credits the seller with winning price minus the tiered commission and stores commission_amount on the auction settlement record.
E2E: a seller whose auction sells for $150 receives $142.50.
features.notes: Replaces the flat COMMISSION_RATE (5%). The spec says 'greater than $10,000' for 1% and leaves $9,999.01-$10,000 undefined; exactly $10,000 is treated as 1%. Tiers use whole-dollar boundaries with the lower bound inclusive.
